items.title: Qwen 3.8 Max (Final Version Review & Free Ways): Okay, it's ACTUALLY a TOP MODEL!
items.summary:
In this video, I'll be telling you about the official launch of Qwen 3.8 Max, Alibaba's new 2.4 trillion parameter flagship model that beats Opus 4.8 on most benchmarks, costs a fraction of the price, and is going fully open weight next week.

--
Key Takeaways:
🚀 Qwen 3.8 Max is now officially launched, a 2.4T parameter MoE model with a 1M token context window and native multimodality.
🔓 The full open weights drop next week, along with a smaller Qwen 3.8 27B model for local use.
🤖 Qwen showcased 10+ days of fully autonomous coding, from empty folder to production, with the complete trace published on GitHub.
📊 It tops PaperBench and Terminal Bench 2.1, beating both Opus 4.8 and Fable 5, and is the best computer use model on OSWorld-Verified.
🏆 On my KingBench, it holds second place overall at 81.25%, just behind Fable 5 and above Opus 4.8.
💸 API pricing is just $2/M input and $6/M output, with implicit caching at $0.25/M, a fraction of what closed labs charge.
🆓 You can use it for free
items.author: AICodeKing
items.transcript: [music] Hi, welcome to another video. So, Quen 3.8 Max has finally been launched officially. The preview phase is over. The model is out of preview and QN is calling it their most capable model to date. On top of that, they have also confirmed that the open weights of QN 3.8 Max will be released next week and a smaller QN 3.827B model is also going open weights alongside it. So, there's a lot to talk about here. Let's get right into it. First, let me quickly recap what this model is in case you're new here. QN 3.8 Max is Alibaba's new flagship. It's a massive 2.4 trillion parameter sparse mixture of experts model with a 1 million token context window. And it's natively multimodal, so it handles text, images, video, and documents. It also supports both the OpenAI and the anthropic API protocols, which means you can plug it into pretty much any tool, including clawed code. Now, with the official launch, they're positioning it as a new bar for coding and co-work. And they're highlighting some pretty wild stuff in the announcement. The first thing is autonomous coding. They're claiming 10 plus days of self-evolving development where the model goes from an empty folder to production without any handholding. And they've actually published the complete project trace on GitHub. So, you can go and look at what it did over those 10 days. That's a nice touch because most labs just make these claims without showing the receipts. They're also talking about long horizon mastery with system level autonomous planning and closed loop adaptive learning. They mention things like 500 plus turns of chip design optimization and a 365day e-commerce strategy simulation. And then there's the native multimodal intelligence part where vision isn't just an input. It's a continuous feedback loop for planning, execution, and selfcorrection. So the model can look at what it's building, see what's wrong, and fix it. This is the kind of stuff that actually matters for agentic work. Now let's talk about the benchmarks they have published because this time we actually have full benchmark tables instead of just claims on the coding agent side. It gets 86.6 on terminal bench 2.1 which is above both opus 4.8 and fable 5 at 84.6 and only behind GPT 5.6 soul on paperbench which is about reproducing research papers. It gets 93 and that's the top score above fable 5 at 88.8 and GPT 5.6 six soul at 945. On Swebench Pro, it gets 67.7, which is close to Opus 4.8 at 69.2, but F5 is still well ahead there at 80. And on Frontier Suite, it gets 73.5 above Opus 4.8, but again below Fable 5. So on the hardcore software engineering stuff, Fable 5 still holds the crown, but QN 3.8 Max is now sitting right around Opus 4.8 level, which is kind of crazy for a model at this price. On the general agent side, it gets 74.8 on co-workbench which is above opus 4.8 and GPT 5.6 soul and just below fable 5. It also gets 52.4 on the agents last exam score which is basically neck andneck with GPT 5.6 soul at 53.6 and way above its predecessor. But the area where this model really sweeps is the multimodal and computer use stuff. It gets 86.1 on OS world verified which is the top score above Opus 4.8 Fable 5 and everyone else. It tops perception bench, URUA for embodied reasoning, chariv for chart reasoning, LVB for long video understanding, and vision 2 web for visual web development. So if you want an agent that can actually see and operate a computer, this is now arguably the best option out there. And the fact that this is coming as an openweight model next week is just amazing. Now, as for my own benchmarks, I ran my Kingbench questions on the official release and the results are pretty much the same as what I got with the preview. It's still sitting at second place on my leaderboard with 81.25% just behind Fable 5 and above Opus 4.8. The eights are still eights. The 10ens on the bow and arrow game, the math problem, and the long horizon agentic task are still 10. So, I won't bore you by going through all of it again. If you want the full test breakdown, that video will be linked below. The takeaway is that the official release is just as good as the late preview builds and all the harness improvements that came during the preview like the better clawed code behavior and the improved tool calling have carried over to the final version. Anyway, now let's come to the pricing because this is where it gets really interesting. The API pricing is $2 per million input tokens, $6 per million output tokens, and just 25 cents per million for implicit caching. Now, compare that to Opus 4.8 pricing and this is a fraction of the cost for a model that trades blows with it on most benchmarks and beats it on my bench. For agentic coding where you burn through millions of tokens in a session, that caching price at 25 is a really big deal. So if you ask me on a pricetoform basis, there's nothing at this level right now. As for access, you can use it for free on Q Studio. So if you just want to try it out, that's the place to go. The API is available on QN cloud and it's also on the token plan as well as on coder encoder work. But as I mentioned in my last video, the QN code free tier is still dead. So don't expect free unlimited usage in the CLI. The free option is QN Studio and the cheap option is the API or the token plan. And then there's the open weights part which is the biggest deal of all. Next week the full 2.4 trillion parameter QN3.8 max goes open weight. Now, realistically, you're not running a 2.4T model at home. But this matters a lot because providers can host it, researchers can study it, and the ecosystem gets a frontier level model that isn't locked behind a closed API. And for those of us who don't have a data center in the basement, the QN 3.827B model is also going open weights, and that's the one I'm really curious about. If it inherits even a decent chunk of the big models capabilities, it could become the go-to local model. I'll be testing that one as soon as it drops, so stay tuned for that. So, what's the verdict? Quen 3.8 Max is the real deal. It's second on my leaderboard. It matches or beats Opus 4.8 on most of the official benchmarks. It's the best computer use model out there right now. And it costs a fraction of what the closed labs charge. And with the weights dropping next week, this is arguably the biggest moment for open source AI so far. I think that the closed labs should be a little worried to be honest. Overall, it's pretty cool. Anyway, let me know your thoughts in the comments.
